actions: Read local requirements, phase plan, acceptance, design and code. No repository edits, builds, QEMU, host USB/module/network/ptrace operations. This JSON is the sole output file.

scope_decision.phase2_original_requirement: Optional Rust server, virtual devices, physical sharing, unified backend interfaces, official Linux USB/IP interoperation; validate upstream limitations individually and do not claim unverified device classes. docs/requirements.md:696
scope_decision.not_a_requirement_to_support_every_usb_c: The original Phase2 explicitly permits unsupported classes with accurate reasons. Rejecting ISO is an honest implemented limitation, not ISO support or a full Phase2 pass.
scope_decision.current_substep: Checked release product change and final matrix are being completed by root. This review neither revalidates nor overrides their runtime verdict.
scope_decision.whole_phase_status: Partial; physical G1/G2 and unimplemented/untested capabilities remain open.
scope_decision.phase3_boundary: Remote credentials/TLS, comprehensive per-user device leases, heartbeats, durable restart reconciliation and full nine-state application session management remain Phase3. Existing trusted-network flags/local UID allowlists and actor states do not satisfy those requirements.

recommended_next_task.title: Determine service-termination behavior, then add cooperative SIGTERM cleanup without claiming SIGKILL recovery
recommended_next_task.classification: Source-identified concrete product lifecycle gap; requires an old-product guest reproduction before a runtime defect verdict
recommended_next_task.priority_reason: The physical service explicitly owns interface/config/alternate restoration but subscribes only to Ctrl-C. A normal service stop using SIGTERM can bypass this restoration. Addressing that control path has more product value than repeating official-client interoperation already proved by Composite.
evidence: crates/rustusb-cli/src/physical_server.rs:95-106 selects only tokio::signal::ctrl_c and then calls server.shutdown
crates/rustusb-cli/src/main.rs:401-410 gives these servers ownership of signal cleanup rather than wrapping them in another termination handler
crates/rustusb-daemon/src/linux.rs:525-540 sends the granted FD then ends the request; no retained grant lifetime monitor here
first_bounded_experiment: After root finishes and freezes the current matrix, run one new isolated QEMU physical/ECM service-termination fixture with the exact current unmodified product.

Establish a real leased non-storage QEMU device and a pending real request or a non-default relevant state; record ordinary-user server PID/starttime, exact generation/node, original drivers/config/alternate and client receipt.

Send SIGTERM only to that validated disposable-guest server PID; observe actual process exit, client disconnect/VHCI state and server independent sysfs/resource state within fixed deadlines. Preserve failure and exact pre-run source/binary snapshots.
Separately terminate with SIGKILL in a distinct bounded run if hard-crash semantics are the next intended scope. Do not infer SIGKILL behavior from SIGTERM or vice versa.
conditional_implementation: If SIGTERM skips cleanup as source suggests, register Unix SIGTERM and SIGINT before accepting work and route either to the existing single server.shutdown cleanup path. Keep cross-platform behavior explicit.
Use the same termination contract for virtual/physical server lifecycle without adding new root authority, arbitrary commands or a second USB engine.

Preserve output-backpressure behavior, existing shutdown deadlines, exact errno, quarantine semantics and original-generation checks. The signal must not drop the cleanup future or falsely report restoration.
recommended_next_task.acceptance: After the focused change, ordinary-user server SIGTERM triggers real cancellation and terminal reaping; client closure is observed; original config/alternate/drivers are independently verified, resources return to zero, and exit/result accurately reflects cleanup. Retain old-product failure and new-product evidence. Run relevant software gates and focused cancellation/output-backpressure regressions; broaden QEMU reruns only for affected product paths.
recommended_next_task.hard_crash_boundary: SIGKILL cannot execute Rust signal handling or destructors. Cross-process ownership supervision or safe explicit administrator recovery must be designed and tested separately; merely adding SIGTERM does not solve hard crashes, helper loss, power loss or durable restart reconciliation.
recommended_next_task.stop_rule: Close the bounded cooperative service-stop gap, record any SIGKILL result and remaining recovery requirement, then move to the separately planned recovery design. Do not create more host-state ptrace permutations or claim full Phase3 complete.

remaining_product_gaps.item: ISO transfer execution and per-packet status/actual/frame semantics
remaining_product_gaps.evidence: wire.rs:141-154 explicitly rejects positive num_packets before allocation; endpoint execution supports bulk/interrupt, not ISO
remaining_product_gaps.qemu_feasibility: A future bounded virtual ISO or QEMU audio fixture is possible, but would require new wire/adapter semantics and vendor allocation/cancellation work; this is not a missing assertion on current supported code.
remaining_product_gaps.verdict: Mandatory long-term capability for UVC/audio support; keep unsupported now. Do not mislabel a rejection test as transfer support or demand all classes merely to close this bounded Phase2 substep.

remaining_product_gaps.item: Exact recovery of originally unbound interface at nonzero alternate
remaining_product_gaps.evidence: worker.rs:1069-1105 temporarily claims/sets/releases; checked-release-design.md:11 records Linux unbind can reset alt0 even after successful RELEASEINTERFACE
remaining_product_gaps.qemu_feasibility: Existing ECM model can establish the case, but generic restoration through ordinary USBFS has not been demonstrated.
remaining_product_gaps.verdict: Real capability gap, not fixed by release_checked or driver-owned CDC recovery. Do not claim a test-only change solves it; any narrow preflight exclusion is safety degradation, not restored support.

remaining_product_gaps.item: Cooperative SIGTERM versus hard-crash ownership and local-driver recovery
remaining_product_gaps.evidence: physical_server.rs:95-106 handles Ctrl-C only; virtual_server.rs:236 likewise. Physical worker uses no_reattach, while daemon linux.rs:525-540 hands off the FD without a retained lifetime supervisor. Linux v6.8 devio.c:1089-1125 closes usbfs state by releasing claims, but has no Rust original-driver/config/alternate journal.
remaining_product_gaps.qemu_feasibility: One deterministic guest-only server termination while real HID/FTDI or ECM is leased can observe kernel/sysfs/FD state.
remaining_product_gaps.verdict: The missing SIGTERM cleanup path is a concrete source-level gap; resulting USB state is not yet runtime-reproduced here. First fix the bounded cooperative shutdown path if reproduced. SIGKILL recovery needs independent cross-process ownership/reconciliation and is not fixed by signal handling.

remaining_coverage_gaps.item: Kernel USB handler internally active/non-cancellable blocking
remaining_coverage_gaps.verdict: Current syscall-entry gates do not prove this. Needs a justified guest-only kernel/QEMU fixture or actual hardware behavior; another ptrace pause before ioctl does not close it.

remaining_coverage_gaps.item: Successful CLEAR_HALT and subsequent endpoint data
remaining_coverage_gaps.verdict: Existing QEMU model supplies a real failure path. A model implementing success is needed before claiming successful endpoint recovery. It is a limited model coverage gap until a product fault is observed.

remaining_coverage_gaps.item: Genuine nonzero error partial data for actual USBFS I/O
remaining_coverage_gaps.verdict: Current controlled adapter tests cover mappings; ECM kernel reports -32 with one opaque byte. Do not call that observed application-level partial payload semantics. Needs a suitable device/model.

remaining_coverage_gaps.item: Two fresh physical IMPORTs racing for the same available generation
remaining_coverage_gaps.verdict: PhysicalBackend::claim changes available to claiming under slot mutex before await, providing a source ownership mechanism. Existing hold-and-busy tests are not simultaneous-first-import evidence; a single bounded race test may be useful, but this is lower priority than explicit official-client interoperation.

Maintain a compact disposition table pointing to existing evidence. R11 remote authentication/TLS belongs Phase3. Composite already has a default-production-log fixed-payload absence regression; comprehensive credentials/serial/config secrecy remains a separate broader audit, not evidence that the existing payload gate is absent.

Do not add arbitrary kernel hooks solely to turn an inherently unavailable hardware gate green.

Do not count TUI, TLS, GUI, packaging, metrics or Windows as implemented in this Phase2 closure.

supersedes.reason: Rev1 omitted the already-tested official CLI cycle in guest-composite-init.sh and incorrectly recommended repeating broad physical/composite interoperability. This correction withdraws that recommendation.

correction.missed_fact: guest-composite-init.sh cycle2 directly runs /usr/bin/usbip attach, port and detach. The client helper observes the port as unmanaged and refuses detach; actual UDP continues and the official owner then detaches.
correction.proven_scope: Independent official Linux usbip attach/port/detach against the actual USBFS Rust Server is already covered, alongside the managed RustUSB client cycle, real cdc_ether/VHCI I/O, exact 38/39B UDP, ownership refusal and original-state cleanup. This read-only correction checks source and markers; original PCAP review is not rerun.
correction.second_missed_fact: Composite tests already scan production server output for both fixed UDP payload markers and require absence at the default log level.
correction.consequence: Do not call physical/composite official-client interoperation or fixed-payload log scanning unimplemented. A virtual HID/CDC direct-CLI variant is optional profile-specific coverage, not a high-priority product task.

optional_lower_priority_coverage.virtual_hid_cdc_official_cli: guest-userspace-init.sh:197-198 currently imports fixed virtual HID/CDC through RustUSB CLI/helper. A direct official-CLI cycle would add profile-specific confirmation, but shared Rust server management and real official-client compatibility already have Composite evidence. It is lower value than process-termination correctness and not a reason to repeat physical/composite runs.
optional_lower_priority_coverage.official_devlist: A direct usbip list invocation can be a small supplemental check if needed; absence of that exact CLI command does not erase existing direct official attach/port/detach evidence.
